forces: Tenor, baritone and orchestra; acoustic scoring unestablished
performers: Enrico Caruso, tenor; Antonio Scotti, baritone; orchestra uncredited
intro: In Act IV of La bohème, back in the attic, the poet Rodolfo and the painter Marcello try to work while thinking of Mimì and Musetta, who have left them, and Marcello keeps finding Musetta on his canvas. Caruso and Scotti sing the duet.

sections.label: A · Rodolfo (tenor) recalls Mimì
sections.mNote: The tenor recalls Mimì’s hands, hair and white neck.

sections.label: B · Rodolfo holds Mimì’s bonnet
sections.mNote: Rodolfo keeps Mimì’s bonnet; Marcello keeps painting Musetta.

sections.label: C · final section of the duet
sections.mNote: The duet ends before everyday conversation resumes.

cues.title: Duet for Rodolfo and Marcello
cues.text: Rodolfo thinks of Mimì’s little hands, scented hair and white neck: “Mimì, mia breve gioventù” — “Mimì, my brief youth.” Beside him, Marcello thinks of Musetta. Tenor and baritone sing together, though each man addresses an absent woman in his own aside.
cues.evidence: Illica and Giacosa, La bohème (1896), Act IV, O Mimì, tu più non torni; the two characters’ asides and Rodolfo’s words. https://www.opera-arias.com/puccini/la-boheme/o-mimi-tu-piu-non-torni/ . Translation ours.
cues.how: About the passage as a whole.

cues.title: Marcello’s monologue, Act IV
cues.text: Marcello says he cannot control his brush. Whether he paints skies, earth, winter or spring, it produces Musetta’s dark eyes and mouth. He calls his own heart cowardly for waiting for her.
cues.evidence: Illica and Giacosa, La bohème (1896), Act IV, Marcello’s parallel monologue beginning Io non so come sia. https://www.opera-arias.com/puccini/la-boheme/o-mimi-tu-piu-non-torni/ . This describes his words across the duet.

cues.title: Rodolfo and Mimì’s bonnet
cues.text: Rodolfo has kept the bonnet that Mimì hid beneath his pillow when she left. He takes it from the drawer and presses it to his heart. “Tutta sai la nostra felicità” — “You know all our happiness.”
cues.evidence: Illica and Giacosa, La bohème (1896), Act IV, Rodolfo’s E tu, cuffietta lieve and its stage directions. https://www.opera-arias.com/puccini/la-boheme/o-mimi-tu-piu-non-torni/ . Translation ours; placed within the later section.
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: After the duet: the mock feast
cues.text: After the duet, Rodolfo asks the time to hide his emotion. Marcello replies that it is yesterday’s lunchtime. Schaunard and Colline arrive with bread and a herring, and the four friends pretend to sit down to a feast.
cues.evidence: Illica and Giacosa, La bohème (1896), Act IV, the dialogue immediately after O Mimì, tu più non torni. https://www.opera-arias.com/puccini/la-boheme/o-mimi-tu-piu-non-torni/ . This is the scene following the recorded duet.

composer.epithet: He held a theatre audience through a scene of a woman at a window, then brought back a tune it had heard before.
facts: Lucca; Milan Conservatory, 1880–83, with Bazzini and Ponchielli
Giulio Ricordi · Luigi Illica and Giuseppe Giacosa · Giuseppe Adami and Renato Simoni
Twelve operas, counting Il trittico as three; a Mass, songs and chamber music
composer.background:
Puccini began at the organ. His family had supplied Lucca with church musicians for generations, and when his father Michele died in 1864, the five-year-old Giacomo was expected to continue the trade. He studied in the town, played in its churches and completed a Mass in 1880. In 1876, however, he had heard Verdi’s Aida in Pisa, and he turned to the theatre. A scholarship helped him into the Milan Conservatory, where Antonio Bazzini and Amilcare Ponchielli taught him composition. His graduation piece of 1883, Capriccio sinfonico, contains the music that later opened La bohème.

He submitted his first opera, Le Villi, to the Sonzogno competition on the last possible day, 31 December 1883; it did not receive a mention. The librettist Ferdinando Fontana arranged a private hearing at the journalist Marco Sala’s house, with Arrigo Boito among the guests. A subscription paid for a performance at Milan’s Teatro Dal Verme the following May. Giulio Ricordi bought the opera and commissioned another. Edgar, first performed at La Scala in 1889, was a failure that Puccini spent years trying to repair.
